2026-06963.headline: Stablecoin freeze power: FinCEN and OFAC send their final rule requiring issuers to be able to block, freeze and reject transactions for White House review
2026-06963.what_changed: On Nov 18, 2026, the White House Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs (OIRA) received FinCEN and OFAC's final rule on anti-money-laundering (AML/CFT) and sanctions compliance programs for permitted payment stablecoin issuers (RIN 1506-AB73), according to OIRA's list of rules under review dated Nov 20. The final text hasn't been released. The April 2026 proposal (91 FR 18582; docket FINCEN-2026-0100), whose comment period closed June 9, would treat issuers as financial institutions under the Bank Secrecy Act and require AML and sanctions compliance programs, including the technical ability to block, freeze and reject transactions.
2026-06963.summary: Under the GENIUS Act (P.L. 119-27), an issuer may issue payment stablecoins only if it can technically comply with lawful orders to seize, freeze, burn or block its coins. The proposal would make that part of ongoing compliance programs: customer identification, suspicious-activity and currency-transaction reporting, sanctions screening, and the ability to block or freeze. OIRA review is normally the last step before a final rule is published. The Act set July 18, 2026 as the deadline for these rules, and because OIRA doesn't post the text under review, any changes from the proposal aren't known yet. Some industry write-ups said freezes would reach tokens traded between holders, but the Act exempts direct person-to-person and self-custody transfers, so that claim isn't supported. Coin Center separately objected (Aug 21) to applying customer-ID rules to secondary-market transactions. On Nov 2, Tether, which issues the USDT stablecoin, said it froze more than $1.5 billion in USDT within 30 minutes of an Oct 29 exchange hack that it said the FBI tied to North Korea; that was the company's own anti-theft step, not a government order, but it shows how fast an issuer can freeze coins. The FDIC's final GENIUS Act rule for the issuers it supervises reached OIRA the same day (tracked separately).
2026-06963.why_it_matters: Freeze and seize capability built into the token itself becomes a legal condition of issuing the main regulated digital-dollar instrument, and the final rule is now one step from publication. That gives authorities a built-in way to stop specific holders' funds on a court or agency order or under sanctions.
2026-06963.why_it_might_not: Freezes would follow a lawful order tied to specific coins or accounts, or sanctions on named parties, comparable to existing bank freezes, and major issuers already freeze voluntarily. The rule doesn't cap or delay ordinary holders' transfers or redemptions.

next_milestone.what: White House review ends and the final rule is published (no date set); the GENIUS Act takes effect Jan 18, 2027

2026-21786.headline: Treasury proposes rules for the outbound investment law (COINS Act): a wider list of countries and technologies, with some deals banned and others requiring notice
2026-21786.org: U.S. Treasury, Office of Investment Security
2026-21786.what_changed: Treasury published a proposed rule (91 FR 67396; RIN 1505-AC94; docket TREAS-DO-2026-0595) to implement the COINS Act, which Congress passed in the FY2026 NDAA on Dec 18, 2025. It would create a new 31 CFR Part 851 to replace the Part 850 program that has applied since Jan 2, 2025.
2026-21786.summary: U.S. persons (citizens, green-card holders, U.S. entities and their foreign branches) would have to notify Treasury of some investments, and would be barred from others, in 'covered foreign persons' tied to countries of concern that work in listed technologies. Covered deals include buying equity or contingent equity, certain convertible or equity-like loans, joint ventures, greenfield projects, directing a foreign person's deal, and some limited-partner stakes in non-U.S. funds. U.S. parents would also answer for deals made by foreign subsidiaries they control. The countries of concern grow from China (including Hong Kong and Macau) to also cover Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Russia and Venezuela 'under the regime of Nicolas Maduro', which Treasury says no longer exists. The technologies grow from semiconductors, quantum and AI (renamed 'super intelligence systems') to add high-performance computing/supercomputing and hypersonics; Treasury's press release also lists biotechnology. The statute exempts bank lending, payment processing and clearing, underwriting, prime brokerage and global custody, plus de minimis deals at amounts Treasury has not yet set. National-interest exemptions are available.
2026-21786.why_it_matters: This is the only live federal framework that requires advance notice for, or outright bans, Americans' investments abroad. It now rests on a statute instead of an executive order, so it is more durable. The proposal widens the countries and sectors covered and lets Treasury add more technology categories through notice and comment. It also reaches indirect routes (fund-of-funds and LP stakes, structures that hide a U.S. person's role) and makes 'reasonable and diligent inquiry' a compliance duty.
2026-21786.why_it_might_not: It is targeted at national security. It covers only specified technology activities by entities linked to six named countries, and it does not limit ordinary payments, bank lending, custody or deposits. Treasury reports only about 100 notifications in roughly 21 months of the existing program. For most Americans it limits nothing about moving or holding money.

fincen-1506-AB60-cdd-revisions.why_it_matters: Account-ownership reporting rules define what banks must know and can share with Treasury about every business account; changes here shape financial visibility.
fincen-1506-AB60-cdd-revisions.why_it_might_not: This is a planned rulemaking listed in an agenda, not a proposal; direction (tighter or looser) is unconfirmed, and agency agendas often slip. The CTA reporting regime itself was sharply narrowed in 2025.

Changes in the final version aren't known yet. This is a burden-reduction measure, not a new reporting or transfer limit: the $10,000 currency transaction report and suspicious-activity reporting aren't changed by it.
fincen-1506-AB72-amlcft-program-nprm.why_it_matters: Sets the baseline for how aggressively banks monitor and report customer activity; a looser regime reduces pressure that drives account closures and transaction friction.
fincen-1506-AB72-amlcft-program-nprm.why_it_might_not: Reporting thresholds (CTR $10,000, SAR) are unchanged by these proposals; FinCEN's own analysis calls the effect reallocative, not a cut in total monitoring.

genius-implementation-2026.headline: GENIUS Act rules move forward: the FDIC sends its final stablecoin-issuer rule for White House review; OCC final rule adopted; Fed proposals open for comment until Nov 30
genius-implementation-2026.org: FDIC; OCC; Federal Reserve Board; U.S. Treasury
genius-implementation-2026.what_changed: On Nov 18, 2026, OIRA received the FDIC's final rule setting GENIUS Act requirements for the stablecoin issuers it supervises (RIN 3064-AG19), according to OIRA's list of rules under review dated Nov 20; the FDIC's agenda entry says the rule covers capital, liquidity risk management, reserve assets and operational and compliance standards. Earlier: the OCC adopted its final GENIUS rule (new 12 CFR Part 15) on Oct 21, 2026, effective Jan 18, 2027; the Fed proposed reserve, capital and application rules on Sept 24, 2026, with comments due Nov 30; and Treasury's section 3 proposal (2026-16796) closed for comment on Oct 19, 2026.
genius-implementation-2026.summary: From Jan 18, 2027, only licensed issuers may issue payment stablecoins in the U.S. Issuers must back coins fully with reserves such as short-term Treasury bills and meet redemption, capital and risk standards. Starting July 18, 2028, digital-asset service providers may not offer U.S. persons stablecoins from issuers that are not permitted. The OCC set BSA, AML and sanctions requirements aside for a separate rulemaking with Treasury, whose final version also reached OIRA on Nov 18 (tracked). The FDIC's final text hasn't been released. Treasury's proposal defines 'issue' to exclude transfers 'required by a lawful order'.
genius-implementation-2026.why_it_matters: This is building a regulated private digital-dollar system in which every compliant token carries freeze capability. It requires reserves in short-term Treasuries, which creates captive demand for government debt but only within the issuer sector.
genius-implementation-2026.why_it_might_not: It is licensing and prudential regulation of issuers. Holders face no new limits on withdrawing, redeeming or moving funds, and the rules include redemption standards.

hr1799-119.headline: House bill to raise cash and suspicious-activity reporting thresholds awaits a floor vote
hr1799-119.org: Rep. Loudermilk (sponsor); House Financial Services Committee
hr1799-119.what_changed: H.R. 1799, the Financial Reporting Threshold Modernization Act, was reported with an amendment on Mar 19, 2026 (H. Rept. 119-556; Union Calendar No. 478). No later floor action was confirmed.
hr1799-119.summary: As reported, the bill would raise the $10,000 cash-reporting threshold for non-financial businesses (31 U.S.C. 5331) to $30,000. It would also raise SAR thresholds from $5,000 to $10,000 and from $2,000 to $3,000, raise MSB-definition thresholds from $1,000 to $3,000, and index all of them to inflation every 5 years. It also directs a Treasury review of CTR and SAR requirements. This researcher did not verify the exact change to the bank CTR threshold under 31 U.S.C. 5313 in the reported text. A June 2026 House hearing, including Cato Institute testimony, also pushed to raise or repeal Bank Secrecy Act reporting thresholds.
hr1799-119.why_it_matters: It would roll back cash surveillance that has grown in real terms because the thresholds were never indexed. It also cuts against the GTO trend of lowering thresholds.
hr1799-119.why_it_might_not: It has not passed the House and has no Senate action, and it expires on Jan 3, 2027.

hr8995-119.headline: House bill would raise the remittance tax from 1% to 25% and drop the bank-account and card exemptions
hr8995-119.org: Rep. Chip Roy (sponsor); House Ways and Means Committee
hr8995-119.what_changed: H.R. 8995, the 'REMITTANCE Act', was introduced May 21, 2026 and referred to Ways and Means. No later action could be confirmed.
hr8995-119.summary: The bill would change the sec. 4475 rate from 1% to 25%. It would strike the subsections that limit the tax to cash-funded transfers and exempt account- and card-funded ones, so on its face it would reach any consumer remittance transfer as defined in the Electronic Fund Transfer Act. U.S. citizens could claim an income-tax credit only for tax paid on transfers for business or travel purposes.
hr8995-119.why_it_matters: A 25% tax on consumer transfers abroad would work as a strong financial barrier to sending personal funds overseas, even though it is not a formal limit. It is the most aggressive official proposal on outbound transfers found in this scan.
hr8995-119.why_it_might_not: It is a single-sponsor bill with no confirmed cosponsors, hearing or markup, and it dies when the 119th Congress ends on Jan 3, 2027. The tag #7 is approximate: the bill taxes transfers rather than capping them.

intl-ecb-digital-euro-holding-limits.summary: The digital euro would carry a per-person cap on holdings, explicitly to stop savers moving too much money out of banks in a crisis. The ECB says limits up to EUR 3,000 would cause no aggregate outflow under normal conditions; Cipollone said figures were illustrative, not a decision. Reporting says the cap will not be written into the law itself; the ECB would recommend it and legislators would decide, and Parliament wants the Commission to set it on ECB advice while the Council wants to set it itself. The ECB is also exploring conditional payments as a future feature. The seventh round of political talks (trilogue) began Nov 18 and ended at 4:30 a.m. on Nov 19 after more than 14 hours without a deal, ANSA reported; sticking points included whether people hit by other countries' sanctions that the EU doesn't recognize can still use the digital euro, and the fee model for merchants. Negotiators plan another meeting, and the Irish presidency still aims for a political agreement by the end of 2026. Reports said the method for setting the holding limit, and who sets it, is still open. CriptoNoticias reported on Nov 17 that without a deal this year the file would pass to the next Council presidency, which could push the launch to 2030.

crypto-exchange-withdrawal-pauses-2026-1.headline: Crypto platforms keep pausing withdrawals after hacks, threats and vendor failures: Lighter reopened the same day after a theft, while South Korea's Gopax was still shut on Nov 19
crypto-exchange-withdrawal-pauses-2026-1.org: Binance; Gopax (South Korea); Mercado Bitcoin, Nubank and Mercado Pago (Brazil)
crypto-exchange-withdrawal-pauses-2026-1.who: Private cryptocurrency exchanges and fintech apps
crypto-exchange-withdrawal-pauses-2026-1.what_changed: On Nov 16, 2026, Lighter, an Ethereum-based crypto derivatives exchange, paused withdrawals and new liquidity pools after an attacker drained funds from one trader's account, then reopened deposits and withdrawals later that day once its Security Council turned off the 'Guardian' safety mode; Lighter said it returned about $5 million in USDC to the trader. Its postmortem blamed API keys leaked through the trader's own custom signing software, not Lighter's code, and on-chain analysts estimated the amount taken at about $10.4 million to $15.5 million. In South Korea, Gopax, which halted trading, deposits and withdrawals on Nov 6 after hacking threats, was still shut on Nov 19 with no restart date; the Seoul Economic Daily reported that holders of 24 tokens that, among South Korea's major exchanges, trade only on Gopax have no domestic venue to sell them, and some barely trade abroad; it postponed planned final trading of five tokens being delisted, and data a lawmaker obtained from the Financial Supervisory Service showed a separate Sept 8 data breach had exposed the personal information of 2,009 people, up from the 9 Gopax first reported. Earlier: Brazil's Nubank and Mercado Pago paused some crypto transfers on Nov 6 after problems at outside providers; Uphold said withdrawal delays that began around Nov 4 came from a disruption at an outside transaction-monitoring partner, and its status page showed them mostly resolved by Nov 10; Binance, hacked for about $6.3 billion on Oct 29, has reopened withdrawals in phases since Nov 1; and Brazil's Mercado Bitcoin halted withdrawals Nov 2 after about $40 million was drained.
crypto-exchange-withdrawal-pauses-2026-1.summary: These were company decisions after thefts, threats or vendor failures, not government limits on customers' money, and Lighter's pause lasted only part of a day. Binance said it would cover losses, and Binance is Gopax's majority shareholder. Stablecoin issuers Tether and Circle froze wallets holding coins stolen from Binance, about $3 billion in total, which shows the freeze ability that U.S. rules will require issuers to have for lawful orders. The Brazil and Uphold delays show that a failure at an outside data or compliance vendor can stop transfers even when the platform itself isn't hacked. Binance.US, a separate U.S. platform, said it was not affected by the Binance hack. Since the Lighter incident, the exchange requires a wallet signature for transfers into public pools. On Nov 20, South Korea's Financial Supervisory Service told all 28 registered crypto firms to apply its emergency security guideline (tracked under Around the world); we found no report of a Gopax restart.
crypto-exchange-withdrawal-pauses-2026-1.why_it_matters: Withdrawal pauses at big platforms can spread fear and claims that capital controls are starting. The stablecoin freezes show how quickly issuers can block coins, an ability U.S. rules will soon require, and the Brazil cases show how one outside compliance vendor can halt transfers at several firms.
crypto-exchange-withdrawal-pauses-2026-1.why_it_might_not: The pauses were company security or technical steps at platforms outside the U.S., not government orders to limit customers' money; Lighter reopened the same day, Nubank the same night, and Binance has been reopening in phases.

2026-22809.headline: FinCEN and the Fed drop a 2020 plan to cut the record-keeping threshold for transfers abroad from $3,000 to $250
2026-22809.org: FinCEN (Treasury) and the Federal Reserve Board
2026-22809.what_changed: FinCEN and the Fed announced on Nov 6, 2026, that they were withdrawing their October 2020 joint proposal (85 FR 68005; RIN 1506-AB41). The withdrawal notice (FR Doc 2026-22809) was published in the Federal Register on Nov 9, making the withdrawal official.
2026-22809.summary: The 2020 proposal would have lowered, from $3,000 to $250, the amount at which banks and money transmitters must collect and keep sender and recipient details on funds transfers that begin or end outside the U.S., and the amount at which FinCEN's travel rule requires passing those details along the payment chain. It also would have stated that these rules cover crypto and digital assets with legal-tender status. The agencies said they received nearly 3,000 comments, mostly opposed; that more than five years had passed; and that crypto markets and laws, including the GENIUS Act, have changed. They said no similar final rule will be issued without a new chance for public comment. The $3,000 threshold stays in place.
2026-22809.why_it_matters: It retires a long-pending plan that would have brought far more everyday transfers abroad, such as family remittances, under record-keeping and pass-along requirements, and the agencies committed to new public comment before trying anything similar.
2026-22809.why_it_might_not: The existing $3,000 rules stay in place, and the agencies left room for future changes aimed at crypto. Tighter reporting can still come through other tools, such as geographic targeting orders like the Minnesota and Southwest border orders, or rules to carry out FATF's new payment-transparency standard.

fincen-9714-mexc-global.what_changed: FinCEN's Nov 6 order was published in the Federal Register on Nov 10, 2026 (FR Doc 2026-22962, 91 FR 72420), which starts its 30-day clock: it takes effect Dec 10, 2026. From then, covered U.S. financial institutions may not process transmittals of funds to or from MEXC Global, a Seychelles-incorporated crypto exchange that FinCEN found to be of primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance under section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act.
fincen-9714-mexc-global.summary: The published order says MEXC processed more than $1 billion a day as of June 2026 and operates in more than 170 countries through current or former affiliates in the Seychelles, Estonia, Switzerland, the United Kingdom and Singapore. Treasury says MEXC Global, one of the 20 largest crypto exchanges in the world, facilitated at least $16 billion in transactions tied to Iranian, North Korean and Russian sanctions evasion and to cybercrime between May 2021 and May 2026. The order covers MEXC's subsidiaries, branches, offices and successors outside the U.S., and it explains how covered institutions should handle crypto that arrives from MEXC when it can't be rejected. It doesn't change existing reporting or sanctions duties and has no end date. MEXC said its operations were normal and that it had started an independent review of its anti-money-laundering and sanctions controls. The order names one foreign company; it doesn't limit transfers to other platforms or ordinary transfers abroad. On Nov 18, MEXC shut down its Visa-linked Global Card, which let users outside the U.S. spend the USDT stablecoin; it had paused the card on Nov 14, citing changes at its outside card issuer, and didn't say whether FinCEN's order played a part. U.S. residents were already barred from the card.
fincen-9714-mexc-global.why_it_matters: It's a direct ban on a channel for moving money, imposed with an anti-money-laundering power rather than ordinary sanctions, against one of the world's larger crypto exchanges. It shows how quickly U.S. institutions can be cut off from a named platform.
fincen-9714-mexc-global.why_it_might_not: It covers one offshore exchange that Treasury ties to sanctions evasion and cybercrime. Ordinary transfers abroad and other platforms aren't affected, and FinCEN has used similar orders against other named foreign institutions.

intl-imf-stablecoin-flows-capital-contro.what_changed: An Oct 1, 2026 IMF working paper (No. 2026/211) estimated stablecoin flows for 188 countries, and an Oct 8 departmental paper (No. 2026/021) set out initial policy considerations for foreign-currency stablecoins. intl-imf-stablecoin-flows-capital-contro.summary: The working paper estimates $21.4 trillion in gross international stablecoin flows from 2018 to 2025, with emerging and developing economies holding three quarters of stablecoins. intl-imf-stablecoin-flows-capital-contro.why_it_matters: It documents people turning to stablecoins when their countries restrict money leaving, which could push governments to aim future capital controls at stablecoin flows.
intl-imf-stablecoin-flows-capital-contro.why_it_might_not: It's research and early policy thinking about other countries, not a recommendation to limit Americans, and the U.S. already regulates its own dollar stablecoins under the GENIUS Act.

us-stocks-selloff-2026-11-05.summary: Trading continued normally the next day, and we found no reports of U.S. banks limiting withdrawals or of funds limiting redemptions. A falling stock market isn't a capital control: it changes what investments are worth, not whether people can withdraw or move their money. Stocks fell again on Monday, Nov 16, a third straight loss for the S&P 500, which dropped 1.9%; the Nasdaq fell 2.5% and the Dow 739 points (1.4%), led by chip stocks. On Tuesday, Nov 17, the S&P 500 fell another 1.03% to 7,340.53, a fourth straight loss and its lowest close since late July; the Dow lost 848.75 points (1.64%) and the Nasdaq 0.74%. On Wednesday, Nov 18, the S&P 500 fell 0.23% to 7,323.63, a fifth straight loss, and the Dow lost 561.25 points (1.11%) as Nvidia shares lost momentum after the chipmaker's better-than-expected results, while the Nasdaq rose about 0.4%. Markets stayed open, and we again found no fund or bank limits on withdrawals. On Thursday, Nov 19, the S&P 500 fell 2.02% to 7,175.83, a sixth straight loss; the Dow lost 1,101.11 points (2.19%) to 49,097.06, its first close below 50,000 since June; and the Nasdaq fell 2.25%, as stocks slid after Anthropic's first day of trading. The VIX volatility index reached close to 29, its highest since March. Money market fund assets were about flat, down $3.58 billion to $7.98 trillion in the week to Nov 18. Markets stayed open, and we again found no fund or bank limits on withdrawals.
us-stocks-selloff-2026-11-05.why_it_matters: Sharp market drops can strain funds and lenders and often fuel claims that limits on withdrawals are coming, so this monitor watches for redemption gates, liquidity fees or bank limits during selloffs.
us-stocks-selloff-2026-11-05.why_it_might_not: Prices rise and fall, and a one-day drop doesn't limit anyone's access to their money. Markets stayed open, and the Nasdaq and S&P 500 partly recovered the next day.

dol-1210-AC38-401k-alternatives.org: Department of Labor (Employee Benefits Security Administration)
dol-1210-AC38-401k-alternatives.what_changed: On Nov 5, 2026, the Labor Department's final rule 'Fiduciary Duties in Selecting Designated Investment Alternatives' (RIN 1210-AC38) arrived at the White House Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs for review, according to news reports citing the office's public docket. This review is the last step before publication; the final text isn't public, and there is no deadline.
dol-1210-AC38-401k-alternatives.summary: The March 31, 2026 proposal would give employers and other plan managers a legal safe harbor when they add funds holding alternative assets to 401(k) menus, if they weigh six factors: performance, fees, liquidity, valuation, benchmarks and complexity. Alternative assets include private equity and debt, real estate, commodities, infrastructure, lifetime-income strategies and actively managed funds that hold digital assets. The rule carries out an August 2025 executive order (EO 14330). It wouldn't require any plan to offer these funds; it deals with how plan managers choose investments and doesn't address withdrawals or rollovers. The proposal notes such assets can carry higher fees and be harder to sell and to price.
dol-1210-AC38-401k-alternatives.why_it_matters: Limits on what retirement savers can hold are one form of financial repression this monitor watches for. This rule moves the other way, making it easier for 401(k) plans to offer assets beyond stocks, bonds and cash funds.
dol-1210-AC38-401k-alternatives.why_it_might_not: It's a legal safe harbor, not a mandate: employers still decide what their plans offer, the final text could change, and the proposal doesn't address withdrawals or rollovers. Funds holding private assets can themselves limit how quickly investors cash out.

foster-real-time-regulatory-study-act-dr.what_changed: On Nov 5, 2026, Rep. Foster released a discussion draft of the Real-Time Regulatory Study Act. It would direct the Federal Reserve Board, working with other financial regulators, to develop, test and publicly release open-source demonstration software that could streamline banks' reporting and give regulators real-time information on the condition of financial institutions.
foster-real-time-regulatory-study-act-dr.summary: A one-page summary lists modules such as regulatory dashboards, automated bank and credit union reports, stress tests on historical and current data, AI risk monitoring, and automated fraud and anti-money-laundering screening. The draft calls for an interim report to Congress within 180 days, a systemwide test within 18 months and a final assessment within two years. According to the summary, no live customer accounts would be used and no actions would be taken based on test results. Foster's release says AI and round-the-clock payment systems could spread financial stress quickly, and that real-time tools could help regulators respond faster and prepare for orderly bank resolutions. It is a draft, not an introduced bill.
foster-real-time-regulatory-study-act-dr.why_it_matters: Real-time data would give regulators a faster view of trouble at banks, such as sudden deposit outflows, and shape how quickly they could respond to a run. Its author is likely to gain influence when his party takes control of Congress.
foster-real-time-regulatory-study-act-dr.why_it_might_not: It's a study of supervisory tools for banks and credit unions, not a rule on customers' accounts. It would use no live customer accounts, and it hasn't been introduced or scheduled for a hearing.

next_milestone.what: Possible formal introduction; none scheduled (the new Congress convenes Jan 3, 2027)

foster-real-time-regulatory-study-act-dr.linked_bills_or_rules: None. Separate from the FDIC's provisional-hold proposal; FedScoop reports Foster co-sponsored a separate bill to upgrade regulators' technology that passed the House in September.

intl-asia-market-support-2026-11-06.headline: Taiwan's short-selling limits and South Korea's margin-loan relief take effect after Asian stock markets fell up to 6% following the U.S. drop
intl-asia-market-support-2026-11-06.org: Taiwan's Financial Supervisory Commission and National Financial Stabilization Fund; South Korea's Financial Supervisory Service
intl-asia-market-support-2026-11-06.what_changed: On Nov 9, the steps announced Nov 6 took effect: Taiwan's Financial Supervisory Commission cut intraday short sales of borrowed shares to 3% of a stock's average daily volume over the prior 30 trading days (from 30%) and raised the minimum short-sale margin from 90% to 130%, and South Korea exempted brokerages from the 140% minimum collateral ratio on margin loans through Jan 31. Asian markets were mixed that day: MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan was up 0.8% by midday after falling 4.6% the week before, while South Korea's KOSPI closed 0.8% lower. On Nov 6, Japan's Nikkei had fallen 5.96%, South Korea's KOSPI 6.02% and Taiwan's index 4.5%, Korea's exchange paused trading for 20 minutes under its automatic circuit breaker, and Taiwan's National Financial Stabilization Fund authorized buying stocks, its 10th activation.
intl-asia-market-support-2026-11-06.summary: The selloff followed the Nov 3 U.S. midterm elections and worries that the results would slow AI and data center spending. The steps aim to support prices: buying stocks, curbing bets on falling prices, and easing margin calls so fewer investors are forced to sell. Several people told Reuters that Taiwan's Finance Ministry asked state-owned banks to support the market. Taiwan's fund cited record foreign selling of NT$994 billion in October and NT$524 billion more in November through Nov 6. None of these steps limits bank withdrawals, currency exchange or moving money abroad. On Nov 12, Taiwan's Financial Supervisory Commission said it has set no end date for the short-selling limits and reviews them daily; short sales of borrowed shares fell to 1.7% to 2% of main-board turnover on Nov 9-11, from 2.97% on Nov 6. Taiwan's main index fell 2.63% on Nov 12. Markets fell again this week: Taiwan's main index dropped about 6% on Nov 16 and 2.31% on Nov 17, when dealers said the stabilization fund appeared to be buying, and South Korea's KOSPI fell 2.59% on Nov 17 to 4,968.48, below 5,000 for the first time in nine months. Some Korean retail investors called for a temporary short-selling ban, but we found no new government limit.
intl-asia-market-support-2026-11-06.why_it_matters: It shows how quickly governments step into markets during a sharp selloff, including limits on one kind of trade. Steps like these can fuel claims that broader limits on selling or moving money are next.
intl-asia-market-support-2026-11-06.why_it_might_not: State stock-buying funds and short-sale curbs are familiar, temporary tools in Asian markets. They don't stop investors from selling shares they own or from moving their money, and the U.S. has no similar state stock fund.
intl-asia-market-support-2026-11-06.us_link: No direct link. U.S. exchanges use automatic, marketwide circuit breakers, and the SEC last temporarily banned short selling, of financial stocks, in September 2008. We found no U.S. market-support steps after the Nov 5 drop.

next_milestone.what: South Korea's margin-loan relief ends Jan 31 unless changed; Taiwan's short-selling limits have no end date and are reviewed daily; watch for any step that limits selling shares or moving money

japan-shinkin-outage-2026-11-06.headline: Equipment failure halts ATMs and counter service at 128 small banks in western Japan for about six hours; not a cyberattack
japan-shinkin-outage-2026-11-06.org: Shinkin Central Bank and Shinkin Kyodo Center (Japan)
japan-shinkin-outage-2026-11-06.what_changed: Around 1:30 p.m. on Nov 6, a failure in the shared network system for shinkin banks left customers of 128 institutions, mainly in western Japan, unable to use ATMs or make deposits and withdrawals at branch counters; online banking was also reported down. Shinkin Central Bank and the Shinkin Kyodo Center said service was fully restored shortly after 7 p.m. the same day and that the cause was an equipment malfunction, not a cyberattack.
japan-shinkin-outage-2026-11-06.summary: Shinkin banks are community lenders that share a central computer system; the outage hit the network's western center, while banks in eastern Japan worked normally. Some outlets called it a banking crisis, but it was a technical failure lasting about six hours, not a government action or a bank run. It has no link to U.S. banks.
japan-shinkin-outage-2026-11-06.why_it_matters: Outages that stop people from getting cash, even briefly, can spark rumors of frozen accounts, so it helps to know when a halt is technical.
japan-shinkin-outage-2026-11-06.why_it_might_not: It was a hardware fault fixed the same evening, at small regional banks in another country, with no government order involved.

next_milestone.what: None scheduled; the banks pledged steps to prevent a repeat

paraguay-ueno-bank-resolution-2026-11.headline: Paraguay's central bank plans to move failed Ueno Bank's accounts to several banks in lots after finding about $600 million in sound assets; covered savers have received advances of up to about $19,000
paraguay-ueno-bank-resolution-2026-11.org: Banco Central del Paraguay (Paraguay's central bank) and its banking and securities supervisors
paraguay-ueno-bank-resolution-2026-11.what_changed: On Nov 12, 2026, central bank president Jorge Schreiner said auditors had preliminarily found about $600 million in sound assets at Ueno, more than the bank owes to pension funds such as the Social Security Institute (IPS), whose deposits and investments there total about $516 million. After a review of 8 to 10 days to draw up an 'exclusion balance' of sound assets against liabilities, the central bank plans to tender Ueno's assets and deposits in lots to several local banks, so no single bank takes on more than it can handle, with the Deposit Guarantee Fund able to cover any gap. If accounts move before pending payouts are made, their holders would become customers of the receiving bank instead of being paid out. Pension funds have legal priority. This follows the Nov 11 completion of advances of up to 40 monthly minimum wages (about $19,000) to all 1,812,348 savers the fund covers. On Nov 16, ABC Color reported that the central bank said all eligible savers had now been credited the advances, about $645 million in total, though some accounts, mainly savings certificates, were still being verified. The legal 15-day deadline to prepare the 'exclusion balance' separating Ueno's sound assets and liabilities fell on Nov 16; the central bank then plans to invite the banks and finance companies that fund the deposit guarantee to bid for parts of Ueno's portfolio, using the proceeds to pay the rest of the guarantee and the pension funds. A central bank director said the aim is a full diagnosis by the end of November.
paraguay-ueno-bank-resolution-2026-11.summary: Paraguay's central bank put Ueno, a digital lender that said it had about 3 million customers, into resolution (a state-run wind-down) on Nov 3 after its solvency ratio fell below half the legal minimum, freezing accounts except for guarantee-fund payouts. AFP reported that Ueno held about $2.8 billion when it was taken over, so the advances cover only part of the money at the bank. The fund's limit is 75 monthly minimum wages (about $37,000) per depositor; EFE reported that payments up to that limit are to be extended from the week of Nov 16, and officials haven't said what happens to balances above it. The guarantee excludes the bank's directors and shareholders, and investors in Ueno's money funds, which aren't bank deposits, are still waiting for a decision on their money. Paraguay's Senate removed President Santiago Peña on Nov 6 over his links to the bank, and prosecutors are investigating.
paraguay-ueno-bank-resolution-2026-11.why_it_matters: It shows in real time what a large bank failure can mean for savers: accounts frozen, covered money returned in stages over about a week, and larger balances and investment funds tied to the bank left waiting. That is the kind of situation U.S. failed-bank rules, such as the FDIC's pending 'provisional hold' proposal for the largest banks, are designed to handle.
paraguay-ueno-bank-resolution-2026-11.why_it_might_not: It is one failed bank in another country, handled under Paraguay's own deposit-guarantee law, and every covered saver has received an advance. In the U.S., deposits are insured up to at least $250,000 per depositor at each FDIC-insured bank, and the FDIC's list shows no U.S. bank failures since Sept 25.

next_milestone.what: Bidding for Ueno's sound assets and deposits among the banks and finance companies that fund the deposit guarantee; the central bank aims for a full diagnosis by the end of November (stated aim)

intl-china-market-support-2026-11.headline: China pauses new stock listings and large share sales by big shareholders, and makes stock-market stability a top task after a tech-stock slide
intl-china-market-support-2026-11.org: China Securities Regulatory Commission and the State Council (China's cabinet)
intl-china-market-support-2026-11.what_changed: On Nov 6, a State Council executive meeting chaired by Premier Li Qiang called for improving the system for stabilizing the capital market and strengthening the stock market's stability; Chinese media reported on Nov 9 that it was the first time the phrase had appeared at such a meeting. Earlier, on Nov 3, the Financial Times reported, and Reuters relayed, that the China Securities Regulatory Commission had given investment banks informal 'window guidance' to pause initial public offerings and had suspended large share sales by existing shareholders until markets recover; Reuters said it couldn't verify the report. On Nov 2, the securities regulator eased its rules on company share buybacks, and the central bank made a lending program that funds buybacks long-term.
intl-china-market-support-2026-11.summary: China's blue-chip CSI 300 index fell 8.5% in October, its worst month in more than a decade, and the STAR 50 index of tech shares is about 40% below its July peak. Because the pauses were given as informal guidance rather than published rules, their exact scope and end date aren't public. China already limits how much money its people can move abroad, including a $50,000 yearly cap on individuals' U.S. dollar purchases. The reported steps restrict new share supply and selling by big holders; we found no reports of limits on ordinary investors selling shares or withdrawing bank deposits.
intl-china-market-support-2026-11.why_it_matters: It's a live example of a government limiting who can sell shares during a market slide, close to the limits on selling financial assets this monitor watches for. It came days after Taiwan and South Korea took their own market-support steps.
intl-china-market-support-2026-11.why_it_might_not: It's in China, which already tightly controls money leaving the country, and it targets new listings and large sales by big shareholders, not ordinary investors or bank deposits. It was given as informal guidance, and its scope hasn't been published.
intl-china-market-support-2026-11.us_link: No direct link. We found no U.S. step to pause listings or limit share sales; U.S. exchanges rely on automatic, marketwide circuit breakers.

intl-lebanon-withdrawal-limits-2026-11.headline: Lebanon raises monthly withdrawal limits on dollar deposits frozen since 2019 from Dec 1, and talks with the IMF on a law to repay deposits make some progress
intl-lebanon-withdrawal-limits-2026-11.what_changed: After an IMF staff visit to Beirut on Nov 10-13, 2026, the IMF said there was progress in clarifying the approaches under consideration, but that more work is needed to agree on a bank-restructuring strategy, including criteria to maximize deposit repayments and a draft deposit-recovery law, now before Parliament, that respects the order in which losses are absorbed. Finance Minister Yassine Jaber said a small committee of the government, the central bank and the IMF will try to finish the law's wording before the end of the year, aiming for a law ready to apply before March 2027 and an IMF program in the first quarter of 2027. Separately, from Dec 1 the central bank's Nov 3 circulars raise the monthly amounts depositors can draw from frozen dollar accounts.
intl-lebanon-withdrawal-limits-2026-11.summary: Lebanese banks have limited depositors' access to their dollar savings since the 2019 financial collapse. On Nov 3, 2026, Banque du Liban issued Intermediate Circulars 780 and 781, raising the monthly amounts eligible depositors can draw from frozen dollar accounts to $1,200 from $1,000 under Basic Circular 158, and to $600 from $500 under Basic Circular 166; the cash portions stay at $800 and $400, and the increases apply only to card payments at points of sale. The changes take effect Dec 1, 2026 and run until June 30, 2027 unless modified or renewed, and amounts paid will be deducted from any future repayment under the deposit law. Jaber said that around 90% of depositors could get their money in cash or 'fresh' dollars in a first phase, with remaining deposits handled through central-bank bonds paid in later stages; he said details are still being worked out. According to a Lebanese news analysis, the circulars have cost the central bank about $6.1 billion since they began.
intl-lebanon-withdrawal-limits-2026-11.why_it_matters: Lebanon is one of the clearest modern examples of long-lasting limits on bank withdrawals: years later, savers can still take out only small monthly amounts. The deposit-repayment law now being negotiated will decide when and how the rest of the frozen savings come back.
intl-lebanon-withdrawal-limits-2026-11.why_it_might_not: It loosens existing limits rather than adding new ones, and it stems from Lebanon's own 2019 banking collapse and frozen dollar deposits, conditions that don't exist in the U.S.
intl-lebanon-withdrawal-limits-2026-11.us_link: No direct link. U.S. deposits are insured up to $250,000 per depositor at each insured bank, and no U.S. withdrawal limits are in place or proposed.

us-sofi-consumer-tokenized-deposit.headline: SoFi Bank rolls out a tokenized deposit for consumers that can be converted to its stablecoin and moved over blockchains 24/7
us-sofi-consumer-tokenized-deposit.org: SoFi Bank, N.A. (a national bank supervised by the OCC)
us-sofi-consumer-tokenized-deposit.who: SoFi Technologies, a digital financial services company whose bank subsidiary is nationally chartered; it reports 15.8 million members
us-sofi-consumer-tokenized-deposit.what_changed: On Oct 22, 2026, SoFi launched SoFi Earn (SOFIE), which it calls the first and only national bank-issued tokenized deposit for consumers. Each SOFIE represents $1 held on deposit at SoFi Bank, earns interest (4.40% APY as of Oct 20) and is FDIC-insured up to the usual limits. Members can convert it 1:1 to SoFiUSD, the bank's stablecoin, to buy crypto or send money to outside wallets over blockchain networks 24/7. SoFi said the product is rolling out to its crypto customers through November.
us-sofi-consumer-tokenized-deposit.summary: A tokenized deposit is an ordinary bank deposit recorded as a digital token on a blockchain. SoFi says SOFIE is a deposit, not a payment stablecoin; SoFiUSD, launched in December 2025, is what SoFi calls the first stablecoin issued by a U.S. national bank. The announcement doesn't describe any spending conditions or programmable rules on customers' money. It is an optional product from one bank and wasn't covered in earlier reports.
us-sofi-consumer-tokenized-deposit.official_acknowledgment: Company announcement; no regulator statement on SOFIE found.
us-sofi-consumer-tokenized-deposit.linked_bills_or_rules: GENIUS Act stablecoin rules (relevant to SoFiUSD); related to the tracked tokenized-deposit projects at Wells Fargo and The Clearing House.
us-sofi-consumer-tokenized-deposit.why_it_matters: It brings bank-issued digital tokens to ordinary consumers, not just businesses, as stablecoin rules take shape. Money on blockchain rails can move around the clock and leaves a lasting record of transfers, and payment stablecoins like SoFiUSD will fall under GENIUS Act rules that require issuers to be able to freeze coins on lawful orders.
us-sofi-consumer-tokenized-deposit.why_it_might_not: It's an optional product from one bank, insured like other deposits, and the announcement describes no spending conditions or limits set by the bank or the government. It doesn't change how ordinary bank accounts work.

intl-bolivia-dollar-deposit-refunds-2026.headline: Bolivia lets new dollar transfers abroad and cash moves through banks run without limits and starts returning $438 million in dollars to lenders
intl-bolivia-dollar-deposit-refunds-2026.org: Banco Central de Bolivia (Bolivia's central bank)
intl-bolivia-dollar-deposit-refunds-2026.what_changed: On Nov 13, 2026, under board Resolution 162/2026, Bolivia's central bank created 'auxiliary liquidity accounts' for all banks and other lenders so that all new U.S. dollar operations through them, covering transfers abroad, cash movements and transfers between lenders, can run without restriction, something it said had been restricted in recent years. It will also return the $438 million in dollar cash that lenders held in their current and reserve accounts at the central bank on Nov 10: $11 million credited Nov 13 to 35 small lenders that mainly serve rural and outlying areas, $43 million on Dec 18 to 18 more, and $384 million on Apr 30 and Sept 30, 2027 to the remaining 8. It now publishes the new accounts' combined balances on its website.
intl-bolivia-dollar-deposit-refunds-2026.summary: A shortage of U.S. dollars has made it hard for Bolivians to withdraw their dollar deposits since February 2023, a freeze on access to savings that the central bank itself calls a 'corralito.' In May 2026 the authorities set a schedule to return dollar deposits in stages by balance size; on Oct 30 the central bank moved up to Nov 5 the repayment of $333 million to households with $10,001 to $50,000, and from Nov 9 lenders manage the reserves on new dollar deposits themselves so those dollars stay available for withdrawals. The remaining stages for individuals, covering balances above $50,000, run from April to July 2027, and companies follow a separate schedule through December 2028. The central bank calls the Nov 13 step a move toward fully normal foreign-currency operations; about 88% of the $438 million goes back to lenders only in 2027. Earlier this month a Bolivian newspaper reported that some customers still had trouble depositing cash dollars, and a former economy minister said dollar transfers and payments remained restricted, with fees of 7% to 10% on some operations.
intl-bolivia-dollar-deposit-refunds-2026.why_it_matters: Bolivia shows how a dollar shortage can turn into years of limits on getting money out of the bank, and how slowly such limits unwind: limits on new dollar transfers are only now being lifted, and older savings are being repaid in stages into 2027.
intl-bolivia-dollar-deposit-refunds-2026.why_it_might_not: This loosens existing limits rather than adding new ones, and it stems from Bolivia's own shortage of U.S. dollars. The U.S. issues dollars and faces no such shortage, and no U.S. withdrawal limits are in place or proposed.
intl-bolivia-dollar-deposit-refunds-2026.us_link: No direct link. U.S. deposits are insured up to $250,000 per depositor at each insured bank, and no U.S. withdrawal limits are in place or proposed.

intl-canada-bill-s8-cash-limits.headline: Canada's government proposes barring most businesses from accepting $10,000 or more in cash and capping crypto ATM use at $1,000 a day
intl-canada-bill-s8-cash-limits.org: Government of Canada (Department of Finance), Senate Bill S-8
intl-canada-bill-s8-cash-limits.what_changed: On Nov 3, 2026, Canada's government introduced Bill S-8, the Combatting Financial Crimes and Drug Trafficking Act, in the Senate, where it awaits second reading. It would bar certain businesses and other entities from accepting cash payments, donations or deposits of $10,000 or more, and bar many financial firms from accepting cash deposits into an account from someone who isn't the account holder or authorized on it. It would also make it a crime to run a crypto ATM without a provincial or territorial license and require licensed machines to keep each user's transactions to no more than $1,000 in any 24 hours.
intl-canada-bill-s8-cash-limits.summary: Canada's Finance Department says cash remains a preferred payment method for criminals and that Canada and Japan are the only G7 countries without a framework to restrict or regulate large cash transactions across the economy. Under the bill, the cash limit would cover one payment or a series of related payments; banks and credit unions are exempt so cash can still be deposited, and cheques, cards and electronic transfers aren't limited. The bill would also let the Finance Minister temporarily suspend registrations of money services businesses (such as money transfer and currency exchange firms), direct Canada's financial intelligence agency to refuse or revoke them, and make regulations to temporarily limit or prohibit certain domestic transactions in prescribed circumstances; the government says these tools can already be used for transactions to or from foreign countries. Crypto ATM rules would start 90 to 180 days after the bill becomes law and the ban on unlicensed machines after 18 months. Similar cash limits were first proposed in a 2025 bill. intl-fsb-turkiye-stablecoin-review-2026-.what_changed: On Nov 11, 2026, the FSB published its second peer review of Türkiye, which examined the country's rules for crypto-assets and stablecoins. It recommends that Türkiye set up a financial stability monitoring framework with specific indicators for risk channels such as cross-border capital flows, establish a dedicated regime for stablecoins, strengthen supervision and enforcement, including against offshore platforms that reach Turkish users, and improve cross-border cooperation and information sharing.
intl-fsb-turkiye-stablecoin-review-2026-.summary: The review says Türkiye has brought much of its crypto market under registration and licensing and already prohibits using crypto-assets for domestic payments, but has no framework for regulating stablecoin issuers. intl-korea-crypto-withdrawal-blocks-2026.headline: South Korea's financial regulator will let crypto exchanges block deposits and withdrawals when a hack is suspected
intl-korea-crypto-withdrawal-blocks-2026.what_changed: On Nov 12, 2026, the FSC said it will issue a no-action letter, a written promise not to penalize, so crypto exchanges can block deposits and withdrawals under certain conditions when a hack or breach is suspected. Current law lets them block only when a hack has clearly happened. Emergency guidelines that apply right away require round-the-clock monitoring; exchanges that can't monitor at all hours must process deposits and withdrawals only during hours when their systems run normally, and tell users in advance.
intl-korea-crypto-withdrawal-blocks-2026.summary: The FSC pointed to the $6.3 billion Binance hack as showing that fast blocking limits harm to users; its release doesn't mention Gopax, which halted withdrawals on Nov 6 after hacking threats (tracked under How banks are doing). The FSC also told exchanges to keep as little of users' crypto online as possible and to carry more insurance and reserves, and said a government Digital Asset Act bill due soon would give crypto firms security standards and liability like financial firms'. FSC Vice Chairman Shin Jin-chang said domestic exchanges hold about 66 trillion won of crypto for more than 10 million users. The letter hadn't been issued as of Nov 12, and the FSC didn't spell out the conditions. On Nov 20 (Korea time), the Financial Supervisory Service met the security chiefs of all 28 registered crypto firms, explained the emergency response guideline drawn up at the Nov 12 meeting and urged firms to apply it; Digital Today reported that the guideline lets firms block deposits and withdrawals in advance when a hack or other cyber incident is suspected. The FSS said it would hold firms strictly accountable for incidents caused by poor checks or ignored weaknesses. Reports didn't say whether the no-action letter had been issued.
intl-korea-crypto-withdrawal-blocks-2026.plain: South Korea will let crypto (digital coin) exchanges stop withdrawals if they suspect a hack. Some exchanges may only handle withdrawals during staffed hours. This is in South Korea, not the U.S.
intl-korea-crypto-withdrawal-blocks-2026.why_it_matters: A government is widening when people can be stopped from taking money out of a platform, even before a hack is confirmed, and limiting some exchanges' withdrawals to staffed hours. It shows how security rules can add new pauses on access to money.
intl-korea-crypto-withdrawal-blocks-2026.why_it_might_not: It's aimed at stopping theft, not at keeping money in the country, and covers crypto exchanges in South Korea, not bank accounts. Blocks would be allowed only under conditions the FSC hasn't published, and the letter hasn't been issued yet.

barr-ai-agents-bank-runs-2026-11-16.headline: Fed Governor Barr warns AI agents could speed bank runs to minutes and calls for guardrails on AI agents acting in customer accounts
barr-ai-agents-bank-runs-2026-11-16.who: Michael S. Barr, a member of the Federal Reserve Board of Governors (speaking for himself)
barr-ai-agents-bank-runs-2026-11-16.what_changed: In a Nov 16, 2026 speech in Milan on AI and financial stability, Fed Governor Michael Barr said AI agents may speed up deposit outflows during stress: they could instantly spot yield differences or stability signals and move funds on their own at high speed, which could make runs unfold in minutes and overwhelm banks' usual liquidity management and regulators' usual response times. He also said major banks report finding AI agents trying to take actions in retail customer accounts without the bank being able to verify authenticity, consent and alignment with the customer's instructions, and he called for guardrails: strict authentication, explicit consent checks for specific actions, technical controls limiting what agents can do, and rules- and values-based constraints.
barr-ai-agents-bank-runs-2026-11-16.summary: Barr said the views were his own. Most of the speech covered the Fed's November Financial Stability Report on AI-related debt, AI in securities trading, cyber risk and consumer protection. He didn't propose any limit on deposits or withdrawals and named no specific policy response to faster runs; his guardrails target AI agents, not customers. The remarks came three days after Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan urged the Fed to lend to banks on weekends and holidays so they can meet outflows as fast as they arise (tracked). Bloomberg reported Barr's warning the same day. At the FinRegLab AI Symposium on Nov 19, Barr said changes underway in Fed supervision and regulation could gradually weaken oversight over time and that inflation is too high; Reuters' report of his remarks didn't mention any deposit or withdrawal limits.
barr-ai-agents-bank-runs-2026-11-16.plain: A Fed leader said AI tools that move money on their own could make a bank run, when many people pull money out at once, happen in minutes. He asked for safety checks on the tools, not withdrawal limits.

He proposed safeguards on AI agents, not limits on customers, and the main idea now circulating among Fed officials, weekend lending to banks, aims to help banks pay depositors faster.

chase-outage-2026-11-16.headline: Software bug at JPMorgan Chase slows or blocks some online, branch and payment transactions for several hours; the bank says it wasn't a cyberattack and customers kept access to their funds
chase-outage-2026-11-16.who: JPMorgan Chase, the largest U.S. bank by total assets, plus customers of other banks and Zelle users who were sending money to or receiving it from Chase customers
chase-outage-2026-11-16.what_changed: On Monday, Nov 16, 2026, a software bug in JPMorgan Chase's on-premise hardware systems slowed its transaction processing. Reports on the outage tracker Downdetector began around 9:53 a.m. ET and peaked near 2 p.m. ET at about 4,800 for Chase. Customers reported trouble seeing balances and making transfers, some app users saw a message that some services weren't available, and some branch transactions failed, including a check deposit in Dallas; an AP photo showed a Chase ATM in Irving, Texas, with a 'not working' screen. Customers of Wells Fargo, Bank of America, U.S. Bank, Capital One, Truist and Zelle also reported problems, but Chase said other banks were affected only when they were party to a transaction with Chase, and Bank of America, U.S. Bank, Capital One, Truist and Zelle said their own systems were working. Chase said transactions were processing normally by Monday evening, and Downdetector showed service back to normal early Tuesday.
chase-outage-2026-11-16.summary: Chase said the problem was a software bug, not cyber-related, and that customers still had access to their accounts and funds, though some transactions took longer than usual; NBC News reported that some customers had trouble getting into their accounts and withdrawing money while it lasted. NBC, citing a person familiar with the matter, also reported that regulators contacted the affected banks right away and found the problem contained. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said investigators didn't believe recent outages were cyberattacks. The outage followed other U.S. tech failures last week, including an air-traffic system problem, which officials said were unrelated. No bank or government set a limit on withdrawals or transfers: it was a technical failure, fixed the same day.
chase-outage-2026-11-16.plain: On Nov 16, a computer bug at Chase, the biggest U.S. bank, slowed or blocked some banking for several hours. It was fixed that evening and was a tech problem, not a limit on people's money.

quote.text: customers still have access to their accounts and funds

chase-outage-2026-11-16.why_it_might_not: It was an explained software bug, fixed the same day, not a policy limit. Chase said customers kept access to their funds, other banks' own systems kept working, and no regulator ordered any hold.

fed-fsr-2026-11.headline: Fed's November Financial Stability Report: banks sound and funding risks moderate, while some private-credit funds still limit withdrawals
fed-fsr-2026-11.what_changed: On Nov 13, 2026, the Fed posted its November 2026 Financial Stability Report, using data as of Oct 28. It found the banking system sound and resilient with high capital, though losses on fixed-rate assets remain sizable, and called funding risks moderate: banks' reliance on uninsured deposits is well below its 2022 peaks. Redemption requests at perpetual-life nontraded business development companies (private-credit funds sold to individual investors) trended lower through the third quarter but stayed elevated, and these funds kept limiting how much investors can redeem each quarter. Money market fund assets stood at a record of about $7.9 trillion, mostly in government funds, and stablecoins stayed at about $310 billion.
fed-fsr-2026-11.summary: The report says the funds' ability to limit redemptions, together with their low borrowing, helped keep the process orderly; these limits are written into the funds' own terms, not imposed by the government. Market contacts surveyed in September and October most often named risks from artificial intelligence, a drop in risky asset prices, higher long-term interest rates, cyberattacks and government debt. The report also notes that hedge-fund borrowing is at its highest since the data began in 2013 and that the GENIUS Act's stablecoin framework takes effect Jan 18, 2027. Separately, New York Fed staff's yearly update (Nov 12) found early signs of modestly weaker bank capital and slightly higher vulnerability to fire sales. Neither publication mentions limits on bank deposits or withdrawals or any emergency measures. Minutes of the Fed's Oct 27-28 policy meeting, released Nov 18, show almost all officials discussed risks if returns on AI investment disappoint, and a few stressed keeping banks' access to the discount window (the Fed's lending window for banks) and other liquidity programs ready; the minutes don't mention limits on deposits or withdrawals.
fed-fsr-2026-11.plain: The Fed, the nation's central bank, says U.S. banks are strong. Some funds that lend to companies still cap how much investors can take out each quarter. Those caps are the funds' own rules, not government limits.
fed-fsr-2026-11.why_it_matters: This is the Fed's twice-yearly checkup on the financial system. Stress in bank funding or a rush to pull money from funds is the kind of trouble that has come before talk of withdrawal limits in the past, so a calm reading matters, and so does the note that some investment funds are already rationing withdrawals under their own rules.
fed-fsr-2026-11.why_it_might_not: The report describes risks, not new rules. It finds bank funding risks moderate, and the withdrawal caps apply only to certain private-credit funds under their own terms, not to bank accounts.

fincen-1506-AB78-cdd-nprm.headline: FinCEN publishes its customer due diligence proposal, with comments due Jan 19, 2027: banks could ask business owners about immigration status when risk warrants, and an ITIN would no longer count as an owner's ID number
fincen-1506-AB78-cdd-nprm.what_changed: On Nov 19, 2026, the Federal Register published FinCEN's proposed rule (FR Doc 2026-23614, 91 FR 74514; RIN 1506-AB78), which starts the comment period: comments are due Jan 19, 2027, on docket FINCEN-2026-0298 at regulations.gov. FinCEN had released the text on Nov 17 with a fact sheet and a Treasury press release, and the OCC, the FDIC and the NCUA issued statements supporting it that day. The proposal would amend the customer due diligence rule for banks and other covered institutions in three ways: (1) state that, where warranted by risk, an institution may obtain more information, including whether the beneficial owners of business customers have lawful immigration status and work authorization in the U.S., when that is relevant to assessing risks such as fraud, identity misrepresentation or sanctions evasion; (2) codify FinCEN's earlier relief (FIN-2026-R001) so institutions no longer have to identify and verify a business customer's beneficial owners every time it opens a new account; and (3) write into the rule the information institutions must collect about each beneficial owner, including an identifying number such as a Social Security number or, for non-U.S. persons, a passport or alien identification number, while specifying that an Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN) is not an acceptable substitute for a Social Security number.
fincen-1506-AB78-cdd-nprm.summary: The rule covers the beneficial owners of legal entity customers, such as companies, which banks have had to identify since a 2016 rule; it implements Executive Order 14406 (May 2026). Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said it cuts unnecessary burden and gives institutions more flexibility, and the Comptroller of the Currency said it would reduce duplicate ownership checks. In the published text, FinCEN says it considered requiring institutions to collect more information from every beneficial owner but rejected that, because the small gain in regulatory certainty would come at significant cost to institutions. FinCEN said it expects ITIN holders who are in the U.S. legally and authorized to work to have other identification, such as a foreign passport or an alien identification card. Nothing in the proposal lets the government or a bank block, delay or cap an otherwise lawful transaction: it changes what banks collect and may ask about business owners. The text can change after comments. FinCEN hasn't said how it relates to the customer due diligence rewrite its regulatory agenda had planned for March 2027 (RIN 1506-AB60).
fincen-1506-AB78-cdd-nprm.why_it_matters: It widens what banks may ask the owners of business accounts, including immigration status when risk warrants, and would stop banks from accepting an ITIN as an owner's ID number, which could make it harder for some business owners to open accounts. It is the first rule change under Executive Order 14406's push for stricter know-your-customer checks.
fincen-1506-AB78-cdd-nprm.why_it_might_not: Customer due diligence is routine anti-money-laundering work, and the proposal also removes a repeat paperwork step. It doesn't let anyone block, delay or cap transactions, extra questions are allowed only when risk warrants, and comments are open until Jan 19, 2027.

next_milestone.what: Comment period closes; a final rule would follow (no date set)

intl-china-ndrc-outbound-investment-2026.headline: China's revised outbound investment rules, effective Dec 1, cover individuals for the first time and widen reporting on money invested abroad
intl-china-ndrc-outbound-investment-2026.org: National Development and Reform Commission (China's top economic planner)
intl-china-ndrc-outbound-investment-2026.what_changed: Newly added to this tracker. On Oct 22, 2026, China's National Development and Reform Commission released revised Measures for the Administration of Outbound Investment, which take effect Dec 1, 2026 and replace the 2017 rules for enterprises. For the first time they expressly include resident individuals as outbound investors: individuals file with the provincial planning office where they are registered or live, and sensitive investments need national approval.
intl-china-ndrc-outbound-investment-2026.summary: According to a CMS law-firm review, the approval and filing system stays largely the same, but reporting widens: a report 10 working days before major preliminary steps on projects of $100 million or more or with diplomatic implications; reports on any reinvestment through controlled offshore companies, whatever the size; completion and exit reports within 10 working days; immediate reports of major adverse events; and an annual report by June 30. Investing without a required approval or filing can bring fines of 0.1% to 0.5% of the amount, rising to 0.5% to 1% plus an order to sell if not corrected, and bans on outbound investment of one to three years. Investments through QDII funds, Stock Connect or the Wealth Management Connect are generally exempt unless they bring control or stakes of 10% or more. Rules on how individuals will actually make such investments, including foreign-exchange rules, haven't been published yet.
intl-china-ndrc-outbound-investment-2026.plain: From Dec 1, people in China, not just firms, must file with the state or get its OK before they invest in firms abroad. The rule does not apply to Americans.
intl-china-ndrc-outbound-investment-2026.us_link: No direct link. The U.S. outbound investment program also covers individuals, but only certain deals in sensitive technologies in countries of concern (Treasury's wider proposal is open for comment until Dec 7). We found no U.S. plan to require approval for Americans' foreign investments in general.
intl-china-ndrc-outbound-investment-2026.why_it_matters: It extends government sign-off and reporting to individuals' investments abroad in the world's second-largest economy, a clear example of tighter controls on money leaving a country.
intl-china-ndrc-outbound-investment-2026.why_it_might_not: China has long controlled money leaving the country, so this formalizes and extends existing rules; portfolio channels such as Stock Connect are generally exempt, and the details for individuals aren't out yet. It doesn't apply to Americans.

next_milestone.what: Revised rules take effect; implementing rules for individuals and foreign-exchange rules still to come

cari-network-tokenized-deposits.headline: Cari, a tokenized-deposit network for regional and community banks led by a former Comptroller of the Currency, says about 30 banks have joined
cari-network-tokenized-deposits.who: Cari Network, founded and led by Eugene Ludwig, a former U.S. Comptroller of the Currency (the national bank regulator) who also founded Promontory Financial Group and the IntraFi deposit network; its design-partner banks include First Horizon, Huntington, KeyBank, M&T, Old National and SouthState
cari-network-tokenized-deposits.what_changed: In a Nov 6, 2026 article by the Global Association of Risk Professionals, Ludwig said 30 banks have joined Cari and another 50 are in active talks, and that he expects the six design-partner banks to be operating on the platform by year-end, able to offer insured deposits in tokenized form. According to the article, Cari launched a basic version of its platform on March 31 and its full product suite on July 31, and the design-partner banks provided its first outside funding, $32.5 million, in September.
cari-network-tokenized-deposits.summary: Tokenized deposits are ordinary insured bank deposits recorded as digital tokens on a blockchain, so they can move between banks at any hour. Cari aims to give regional, mid-size and community banks a shared network like the one the largest banks are building through The Clearing House (tracked). Announcements so far describe no feature that lets a bank or the government set conditions on customers' money. It's a private, voluntary project, not a government rule.
cari-network-tokenized-deposits.plain: Cari, run by a former top bank regulator, helps smaller banks move deposits as digital tokens. About 30 banks have joined, and some plan to start by the end of 2026.

quote.text: tokenizing deposits keeps them in the bank to use, supporting our communities

cari-network-tokenized-deposits.official_acknowledgment: None found; it's an industry project (the American Bankers Association, a trade group, added it to its partner network in July 2026).
cari-network-tokenized-deposits.linked_bills_or_rules: Operates under existing bank rules; the GENIUS Act covers stablecoins, not tokenized deposits. Related: The Clearing House tokenized-deposit network (tracked).
cari-network-tokenized-deposits.why_it_matters: If dozens of regional and community banks put deposits on token rails, programmable bank money could reach ordinary customers' accounts, not just big companies.
cari-network-tokenized-deposits.why_it_might_not: It's a voluntary private network, nothing announced lets anyone set conditions on customers' money, and bank technology projects often launch slowly.

claim-oddlots-yang-capital-controls-2026.headline: Bloomberg Odd Lots guest Tian Yang: managing heavy government debt through financial repression could bring capital controls to Western economies
claim-oddlots-yang-capital-controls-2026.who: Tian Yang, chief investment officer of the VPX fund at the research firm Variant Perception (podcast guest)
claim-oddlots-yang-capital-controls-2026.what_changed: On the Nov 16, 2026 episode of Bloomberg's Odd Lots podcast, 'The Impossible Trilemma That Hangs Over the Nvidia Crisis,' Tian Yang argued that big powers can't fund military and technology races, social spending and sound money all at once. Independent summaries of the episode say he called financial repression, running inflation of 4% to 5% while holding interest rates down, the most likely way to manage heavy debt, named capital controls as its underappreciated risk, and pointed to stablecoins' demand for Treasury bills, bank leverage-rule changes and heavy Treasury bill issuance as tools already in place. One summary site headlined the episode 'Tian Yang Says Capital Controls Are Coming to Western Markets.'
claim-oddlots-yang-capital-controls-2026.summary: We read Bloomberg's episode description and independent summaries, not a full transcript. Parts of the reasoning match the record: the GENIUS Act bars stablecoin issuers from paying interest to holders and requires them to back coins with safe assets such as cash and short-term Treasury bills, so stablecoins add demand for government debt. But the warning is a forecast about what governments might do, not a report of a plan, and we found no U.S. proposal to cap transfers abroad, limit withdrawals or require people to hold government debt. The outbound-investment rules this monitor tracks limit certain tech investments in countries of concern for national-security reasons. Commentary can't raise this monitor's level.
claim-oddlots-yang-capital-controls-2026.claim: Governments managing heavy debt through financial repression are likely to turn to capital controls, a risk that asset owners underrate.
claim-oddlots-yang-capital-controls-2026.claimant: Tian Yang (Variant Perception), on Bloomberg's Odd Lots podcast
claim-oddlots-yang-capital-controls-2026.plain: On a popular Bloomberg podcast, investor Tian Yang warned that deep government debt could lead to limits on moving money. Can't tell yet: it's a guess about the future, and we found no U.S. plan like that.

quote.text: the potential for capital controls

claim-oddlots-yang-capital-controls-2026.linked_bills_or_rules: GENIUS Act stablecoin rules (tracked): issuers can't pay interest to holders and must hold safe reserve assets such as short-term Treasury bills.
claim-oddlots-yang-capital-controls-2026.why_it_matters: Odd Lots is one of the most widely followed finance podcasts, and the argument ties real policies, such as stablecoin rules, to capital controls, so listeners may read ordinary rules as first steps toward limits.
claim-oddlots-yang-capital-controls-2026.why_it_might_not: It's an investor's view of what could happen if inflation stays high and rates are held down, not a report of a specific plan, bill or rule.

dallas-fed-logan-weekend-discount-window.headline: Dallas Fed president says banks must be ready to meet withdrawals as fast as they come and urges the Fed to lend to banks on weekends and holidays
dallas-fed-logan-weekend-discount-window.who: Lorie Logan, President and CEO of the Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas
dallas-fed-logan-weekend-discount-window.what_changed: On Nov 13, 2026, opening a bank-funding conference hosted by the Dallas and Boston Feds, Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan said banks must be prepared to meet outflows as fast as they can arise, and that the Fed should extend discount-window lending (its short-term loans to banks) to weekends and holidays. She said instant payment services such as FedNow can leave banks needing cash overnight on weekends and holidays, when the window is now closed, and that the Fed plans to run its Fedwire Funds service on Sundays and weekday holidays by 2028 or 2029.
dallas-fed-logan-weekend-discount-window.summary: Logan said the views were her own and that the Fed's Board of Governors, not any one Reserve Bank, sets discount-window policy; she said she looks forward to discussing the idea with colleagues. She also urged the Fed to be able to centrally clear its repo operations and to be ready, in extreme cases, to lend to systemically important market utilities such as clearinghouses. She noted that the Fed has removed the overall size limit on its standing repo operations and that 47 depository institutions now use them. The remarks are about making sure banks can always pay depositors; they don't propose any limit on withdrawals.
dallas-fed-logan-weekend-discount-window.plain: A leader at the Fed, the nation's central bank, said banks must be ready to pay customers right away. She said the Fed should also lend money to banks on weekends and holidays.

quote.text: The Fed should extend discount window operations to weekends and holidays.

dallas-fed-logan-weekend-discount-window.why_it_matters: Talk of withdrawal limits tends to grow when banks can't get cash fast enough to pay depositors. Letting banks borrow from the Fed on any day of the week would make it easier for them to handle a weekend rush of withdrawals without limiting customers.
dallas-fed-logan-weekend-discount-window.why_it_might_not: It's one Reserve Bank president's view, not a Fed decision. The Board of Governors would have to approve weekend lending, and no proposal or timeline has been announced.

next_milestone.what: Any Fed Board proposal to open the discount window on weekends and holidays (none announced)

hr9331-119.headline: Committee-approved House bill would let banks hold deposited checks and incoming wires they suspect are fraudulent, for up to 10 days or 45 days if extended
hr9331-119.org: Rep. Young Kim (sponsor); House Financial Services Committee
hr9331-119.what_changed: Newly added to this tracker; its latest action was on Sept 1, 2026. H.R. 9331, the STOP Payments Fraud Act of 2026, was introduced June 18, marked up by the House Financial Services Committee on June 30, and reported to the House with an amendment on Sept 1 (Union Calendar No. 692, H. Rept. 119-792). No floor vote has been scheduled.
hr9331-119.summary: The bill would amend the Expedited Funds Availability Act, under which banks generally must make deposited funds available within one to two business days, and incoming wires by the next business day. Under the reported text, a bank could delay a deposited check or an incoming wire it has 'reasonable suspicion' is false, unauthorized or fraudulent, based on indicators that would lead a reasonable person to suspect fraud, with the reasons given in a notice to the customer. Fed and CFPB rules would set an initial hold of no more than 10 days and an extended hold of no more than 45 days, and could vary them by dollar amount. For wires, no decision may be based on any class of wire transfers or persons, and banks couldn't charge overdraft fees caused by a hold if the customer didn't get written notice. The Fed and CFPB could also name higher-fraud-risk situations in which longer standard holds apply to an account for up to 60 days each time, and could temporarily slow availability for certain classes of checks, such as Treasury checks, during periods of material fraud losses.
hr9331-119.plain: A bill a House committee approved would let banks hold checks and wire transfers (bank-to-bank payments) they suspect are fraud, for up to 10 days, or 45 in some cases. The full House hasn't voted.
hr9331-119.why_it_matters: It would widen banks' power to delay ordinary people's incoming money, including wires that now must be available the next business day, based on a bank's own suspicion. It's the closest thing to a holding period (a Tier 2 signal) we've found in a bill that has cleared a committee.
hr9331-119.why_it_might_not: It's an anti-fraud bill: holds must rest on specific fraud indicators, can't target whole classes of people or wires, are time-limited and come with notice and overdraft-fee protections. It has had no floor action since Sept 1 and dies when the 119th Congress ends on Jan 3, 2027 unless passed, so we count it as Tier 1 friction, not a Tier 2 holding period.

next_milestone.what: House floor vote (none scheduled); the bill expires when the 119th Congress ends unless passed
